topics.title: What McStud Does
topics.summary: The 30-second overview of the program
content: McStud helps you build more complete, better-supported collision estimates and negotiate them with insurers.
It reads estimates, learns from your history, flags operations that are commonly missed, and backs them up with reference documents.
Everything runs locally on your machine. Your uploaded estimates and learned data stay private to your shop.
tips: Work top to bottom through the tabs: Import an estimate, review it in Chat/Ghost, check Scoring and Must-Haves, then Export.
You do not need to use every feature. Start with Import and Chat, then add the rest as you get comfortable.

topics.title: First-Time Setup
topics.summary: Set your Shop Info and Learning Mode before you begin
content: Open the Settings tab and fill in Shop Info: your Shop Name and Your Name.
Shop Name appears on the window title bar and on every document you print or export (checklists, PDFs, tow bills, vendor sheets, and more).
Your Name is used for friendly greetings in the Chat and Welcome screens.
Choose a Learning Mode: Standard uses the pre-trained knowledge base that ships with the app. Personal starts fresh and builds only from your own uploaded estimates.
tips: Standard mode is recommended for most shops and gives consistent results across a team.
Fill in Shop Name first so every document you generate is branded correctly.
warnings: In Standard mode, uploaded estimates use the shared knowledge base but do not modify it. Choose Personal if you want your uploads to build your own private data set.

topics.title: The Interactive Tour
topics.summary: Take the guided walkthrough with Try It mode and achievements
content: The app includes an interactive tour that walks you through each tab with Try It prompts and unlockable achievements.
The tour highlights one feature at a time and lets you try it live before moving on.
You can relaunch the tour any time if you want a refresher.
tips: Use the tour on your first day to see where everything lives.
Achievements are just for fun and to confirm you have tried each core feature.

topics.title: Understanding the Tabs
topics.summary: What each top-level tab is for
content: Export: send finished operations out to CCC/Mitchell, the clipboard, or Excel.
Chat: ask questions, generate a ghost estimate, or read the screen live with OCR.
Guide: this guide, the Excel guide, and Tech Efficiency planning.
Import: upload estimates so the app can read and learn from them.
Reference: pull P-pages, definitions, OEM position statements, and procedures to back up your estimate.
Settings: Shop Info, Learning Mode, and license.
Shop Docs: vendor lists, checklists, tow bills, invoices, parts requests, and more.
Stats: track your performance over time.
tips: Each tab has a help button in its top-right corner for quick context.

topics.title: Uploading an Estimate
topics.summary: How to bring an estimate into the app
content: Open the Import tab and use Estimate Upload to load an estimate file.
The app parses the estimate into structured lines it can read, score, and learn from.
Once parsed, the estimate feeds the Ghost, Scoring, and Reference features automatically.
tips: Upload the insurer's version of the estimate to see what operations may be missing.
After upload, check the Chat > Ghost sub-tab to see how it compares to your history.

topics.title: What the App Learns
topics.summary: How uploads build the knowledge base
content: Each uploaded estimate teaches the app patterns: which operations tend to go together, typical hours, and shop-specific habits.
In Personal mode, uploads are saved to your own private data file and build your personal knowledge base.
In Standard mode, uploads use the shared pre-trained data but do not change it.
warnings: Your uploaded estimates and learned data are your private property. They never leave your machine and are never shared with other users.

topics.title: Duplicate Detection
topics.summary: The app flags estimates you have already uploaded
content: When you upload, the app checks whether the same estimate already exists so you do not learn from it twice.
This keeps your statistics and learned patterns accurate.
tips: If an estimate is flagged as a duplicate, you have likely already imported it.

topics.title: Ask
topics.summary: Ask questions and get answers from your knowledge base
content: The Ask sub-tab lets you type a question and get an answer from the app's knowledge base.
You can ask about definitions, procedures, operations, or how to handle a specific situation.
Try questions like 'What is flex additive?' or 'Check front bumper replace'.
tips: Use the suggested question chips for quick common answers.

topics.title: Ghost Estimate
topics.summary: A shadow estimate built from your learned data
content: The Ghost sub-tab builds a shadow estimate from your learned data and history.
It predicts the operations and hours a complete estimate for this vehicle and damage should include.
The ghost is scored against your history so you can see where the current estimate falls short.
tips: Use the ghost to spot operations the insurer left off before you negotiate.

topics.title: Screen OCR / Screen Monitor
topics.summary: Read CCC or Mitchell live on screen without copy-paste
content: The Screen OCR sub-tab reads what is on your screen in real time, so you do not have to copy and paste from CCC or Mitchell.
As you work in your estimating system, the app can pick up the operations and match reference content automatically.
This feeds the Auto-Matched References in the Reference tab.
tips: Position your estimating window so the operations are clearly visible for the best OCR results.

topics.title: Exporting Operations
topics.summary: Send finished operations to the clipboard or Excel
content: The Export tab sends your finished operations out of the app.
You can copy operations to the clipboard to paste into your estimating system, or export to Excel.
Review your operations before exporting to make sure everything is correct.

topics.title: CCC Web Insert
topics.summary: Automatically insert operations into CCC
content: CCC Web Insert can place operations into CCC for you, so you do not have to type each line by hand.
The automation is scroll-resilient and finds the right spot to insert each operation.
It verifies and retries where needed to make sure operations land correctly.
tips: Let the automation finish before interacting with the CCC window.

topics.title: Auto-Matched References
topics.summary: References matched to your estimate automatically
content: The first Reference tab shows references that were auto-matched to your estimate.
These come from uploading an estimate in the Import tab or from the Screen Monitor reading your screen.
Add the ones you want to your PDF export queue to include them in your backup document.
tips: If you see no auto-matched references, upload an estimate or run the Screen Monitor first.

topics.title: P-Pages, Definitions, OEM & Procedures
topics.summary: Look up supporting documentation
content: The Reference tab includes P-pages, definitions, OEM position statements, procedures, and Included/Not Included details.
Use these to justify operations and explain why they belong on the estimate.
Search for a term or operation to find the backing documentation quickly.

topics.title: Building the PDF Export Queue
topics.summary: Collect references into a single PDF
content: Click 'Add to PDF' on any reference item to add it to the PDF Export Queue.
When you have everything you need, generate the PDF to produce one backup document.
Use Clear to empty the queue and start over.
tips: Give the insurer one clean PDF of supporting documentation instead of loose pages.

topics.title: Vendor Information
topics.summary: Store vendors, sublet shops, and labor rates
content: Vendor Information holds your dealers, tow companies, glass shops, alignment shops, mechanical shops, and sublet/other vendors.
Each vendor can store contacts, phone numbers, emails, address, delivery info, returns info, and labor rates.
Pick a vendor type when adding one. Sublet work uses the specific type (glass, alignment, mechanical) or the Sublet / Other category.
Everything you enter flows onto the Vendor Information document.
tips: Add your sublet vendors here so their contact info is one click away on any job.
Filter the vendor list by type to quickly find, for example, just your sublet shops.

topics.title: Checklists
topics.summary: Built-in and custom shop checklists
content: Shop Docs includes checklists for quality control, blueprinting, health-check scanning, and more.
You can use the built-in checklists or create your own custom ones.
Checklists print with your Shop Name in the header and footer.

topics.title: Tow Bills, Invoices, Parts & Intake
topics.summary: The rest of the Shop Docs document types
content: Shop Docs also generates tow bills, invoices, parts requests, and vehicle intake forms.
Shop Stock Parts, Vehicle Protection, Price Catalogs, and My Docs round out the document set.
All of these pull your Shop Name automatically so your branding is consistent.
tips: Fill in Shop Info once in Settings and every document is branded for you.

topics.title: Estimate Scoring
topics.summary: How complete is this estimate?
content: Estimate Scoring grades an estimate against your history and the knowledge base.
A lower score means operations are likely missing or under-documented.
Use the score as a quick gut check before you send or negotiate an estimate.

topics.title: Must-Haves
topics.summary: The operations that should not be missed
content: Must-Haves are the operations the app believes belong on this estimate and are commonly left off.
They are ordered for negotiation: lower-grade or easier-to-justify items lead, not just the biggest dollar items.
Work the Must-Haves list to make sure nothing important is missing before you finalize.
tips: Lead your insurer negotiation with the items the Must-Haves ordering puts first.

topics.title: Statistics
topics.summary: Track your estimating performance over time
content: The Stats tab tracks your performance: estimates handled, patterns learned, and trends over time.
Use it to see how your estimating is improving as the app learns your shop.

topics.title: Tech Efficiency
topics.summary: Plan and track technician hours
content: Tech Efficiency lives in the Guide tab and helps you plan and track technician hours.
Use it to compare planned hours against actual and keep your techs on target.

topics.title: Shop Info
topics.summary: Your shop and user identity
content: Shop Name brands the title bar and every printed or exported document.
Your Name personalizes greetings in the Chat and Welcome screens.
Type once and it applies everywhere the document supports it.

topics.title: Learning Mode
topics.summary: Standard vs Personal knowledge base
content: Standard uses the pre-trained data that ships with the app and is best for consistent, team-wide results.
Personal starts fresh and builds a knowledge base entirely from your own uploaded estimates.
You can switch modes in Settings at any time.

topics.title: License
topics.summary: Activation and updates
content: Your license is managed in Settings.
The app updates itself automatically when a new version is released, so you stay current.

topics.title: Recommended Workflow
topics.summary: A simple day-to-day routine
content: 1. Import the estimate (or run the Screen Monitor as you work in CCC/Mitchell).
2. Review the Ghost estimate and Estimate Score to see what may be missing.
3. Work the Must-Haves list and pull supporting References into a PDF.
4. Export your operations to CCC, the clipboard, or Excel.
5. Generate any Shop Docs you need for the job.

topics.title: Common Questions
topics.summary: Quick fixes for everyday issues
content: No auto-matched references? Upload an estimate in Import or run the Screen Monitor first.
Documents missing your shop name? Fill in Shop Name in Settings > Shop Info.
Uploads not building your own data? Switch Learning Mode to Personal in Settings.
